corrected_content.problem:
Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x = 1$, $x = 3$, $y =-1$, $y = 1$, $z = 0$, $z = 1$. Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $\mathbf{F}=xz\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+{y}^{2}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k}$, the flux of $\mathbf{F}$ across $S$ can be written as
$$
{∬}_{S}\mathbf{F}\cdot \mathrm{d}\mathbf{S}={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}\hspace{0.167em}\bbox[2pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}}\hspace{0.222em}\text{d}z\hspace{0.222em}\text{d}y\hspace{0.222em}\text{d}x.
$$
What is the missing part of the expression?
corrected_content.worked_solution:
The divergence is
$$\nabla\cdot\mathbf F=\frac{\partial(xz)}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial(y^2)}{\partial y}+\frac{\partial1}{\partial z}=z+2y.$$
The Divergence Theorem therefore makes the missing integrand $z+2y$.
